authority_determination.question: Which source is semantic authority for invalidation conditions, and which is presentation-only?

taxonomy_source.description: Each of the 10 MVP Alphas' own definitional content (2-3 short phrases each). Older, unversioned, carries no source/version/approval_status metadata of its own.
taxonomy_source.api_exposure: GET /api/alpha-library and GET /api/alpha-library/{alpha_id} (comqutor_alpha/api/routes_alpha_library.py, via alpha_loader.load_alpha_taxonomy) -- already faithfully exposes this field for all 10 Alphas, verified unchanged this task.
taxonomy_source.role_this_task: AUTHORITATIVE SEMANTIC SOURCE for the general per-Alpha 'Invalidation conditions' UI section (AlphaCard) -- real product-authored content, but explicitly NOT carrying separate formal approval provenance.

b5_formal_approval_registry.description: A separately-versioned, separately-approved registry (schema_version alpha_invalidation_conditions.v1) explicitly documented in its own header and its own loader's docstring as DELIBERATELY SEPARATE from the taxonomy field above: 'that taxonomy's own invalidation_conditions field is older, unversioned, and carries no explicit source/approval metadata -- it predates this registry and is not treated as a formal Product Owner approval source here.' Historically only A101 carries approval_status: approved (source: John, version: v0.1); every other Alpha is approval_status: not_defined, conditions: [].
b5_formal_approval_registry.consumer: comqutor_alpha/conflict_engine/conflict_evidence_ui.py -> frontend/src/components/ConflictEvidenceSections.tsx -- rendered ONLY for the two Alphas on either side of an admitted main conflict on the Conflict Radar page, already correctly showing an honest 'not yet product-approved' fallback for every non-A101 Alpha.
b5_formal_approval_registry.role_this_task: LEFT COMPLETELY UNTOUCHED. This is the historically-thin, formally-approval-gated registry the Phase-1 demo-readiness audit found -- it is correct and intentional as designed (a narrower, higher-bar, conflict-specific feature), not a bug to fix by loosening its approval gate.

authority_determination.why_A101_historically_had_coverage_while: A101 is the only Alpha that ever went through the B5 formal approval workflow (invalidation_registry.py / alpha_invalidation_conditions_v0.1.yaml) with an explicit source/version/approval_status. This is the registry the Phase-1 audit's 'thin' finding refers to -- it was never a plumbing bug, it is a real, honestly-reported approval gap.
authority_determination.frontend_duplicated_a101_only_registry_d: No hardcoded A101-only dictionary exists in the frontend. The B5 registry that gates A101-only coverage lives entirely in the backend (comqutor_alpha/config/alpha_invalidation_conditions_v0.1.yaml) and is fetched via the existing Conflict Radar evidence-UI endpoint -- the frontend has no second copy of it. The actual gap was: AlphaCard (used by StructureGraphPage, rendered for every Alpha regardless of conflict involvement) never displayed any invalidation-condition section at all, for any Alpha -- not even the honest 'not yet defined' fallback.
authority_determination.answer_to_task_question: The gap was AVAILABLE_BUT_NOT_WIRED (taxonomy content existed and was already API-exposed for all 10 Alphas, but no frontend component outside the narrow Conflict-Radar-pair use case ever consumed it), not a genuinely missing-content or duplicated-registry problem.
authority_determination.single_source_of_truth_applied: Taxonomy -> GET /api/alpha-library -> Frontend (AlphaCard), exactly as directed by the task's Section 6 -- no second hardcoded frontend registry was created.

approval_provenance_discipline.principle: Taxonomy content is real, authoritative product semantics but carries no separate formal-approval marker of its own -- never labelled 'approved' or 'John-approved' in this new UI section.
approval_provenance_discipline.source_transparency_copy: From this Alpha's definition, not this run's analysis.
approval_provenance_discipline.b5_registry_wording_unchanged: ConflictEvidenceSections.tsx's own existing 'approved'/'not yet product-approved' wording for the B5 registry was left completely untouched -- that IS a formally-approved/not-yet-approved distinction and is accurately labelled.
